claim: PSS in ferret visual cortex shares many similarities with primate MT.
source: We have recently demonstrated that area PSS in ferret visual cortex shares many similarities with primate MT (Lempel and Nielsen, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Lempel and Nielsen, 2019)

claim: The same transition from local to global motion processing occurs between ferret V1 and PSS as between primate V1 and MT.
source: Crucially, the same transition from local to global motion processing occurs between ferret V1 and PSS as between primate V1 and MT.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Lempel and Nielsen, 2019) mentioned in the preceding sentence

claim: PSS motion integration develops after postnatal day (P) 40.
source: Using single-cell recordings, we found that PSS motion integration develops after postnatal day (P) 40, during the second week after eye opening, and after the development of direction selectivity.
evidence: Based on experimental data from single-cell recordings presented in the manuscript

claim: PSS motion integration develops during the second week after eye opening.
source: Using single-cell recordings, we found that PSS motion integration develops after postnatal day (P) 40, during the second week after eye opening, and after the development of direction selectivity.
evidence: Based on experimental data from single-cell recordings presented in the manuscript

claim: PSS motion integration develops after the development of direction selectivity.
source: Using single-cell recordings, we found that PSS motion integration develops after postnatal day (P) 40, during the second week after eye opening, and after the development of direction selectivity.
evidence: Based on experimental data from single-cell recordings presented in the manuscript

claim: Maturation of motion integration was reflected in an increasing prevalence of pattern responses.
source: Maturation of motion integration was reflected not only in an increasing prevalence of pattern responses, but also in how responses depended on the exact plaid configuration.
evidence: Based on experimental data from single-cell recordings presented in the manuscript

claim: Maturation of motion integration was reflected in how responses depended on the exact plaid configuration.
source: Maturation of motion integration was reflected not only in an increasing prevalence of pattern responses, but also in how responses depended on the exact plaid configuration.

claim: Visual experience likely plays a role in the development of motion integration.
source: We also provide evidence that visual experience likely plays a role in the development of this process.

claim: V1 responses to plaids undergo developmental changes.
source: Intriguingly, we additionally observed developmental changes in V1 responses to plaids, highlighting the need to consider multiple pathway stages simultaneously during development.

claim: V1 development included a temporary increase in motion integration between P44 and P47.

claim: V1 development included a temporary increase in plaid response strength between P44 and P47.

claim: The temporary increase in V1 motion integration depends on feedback from PSS.

claim: The temporary increase in V1 plaid response strength depends on feedback from PSS.
source: Inactivation of PSS demonstrated that both of these changes depended on feedback from PSS.

claim: Changes in V1 responses are likely to propagate to PSS.

claim: Development of the motion pathway involves coordination between multiple network nodes in a highly dynamic fashion.

claim: Motion processing transitions from local to global computations between V1 and PSS in adult ferrets.

claim: PSS global motion signals emerge a week after the development of V1 and PSS direction selectivity.

claim: V1 responses to more complex motion stimuli change in parallel with PSS development.

claim: V1 responses to more complex motion stimuli change in a manner consistent with supporting increased PSS motion integration.

claim: Development does not just proceed in parallel in different visual areas, it is coordinated across network nodes.

claim: Visual experience had a significant effect on pattern index in addition to age.

Main effects for both factors were significant (main effect age: p=0.02; main effect visual experience: p=04), demonstrating that both contributed significantly to the observed variance in pattern index across cells.

claim: Visual experience impacts the development of PSS motion integration, in addition to the contribution of age.

claim: The strength of plaid responses is positively correlated with pattern index in both primate MT and adult ferret PSS.

claim: PSS inactivation resulted in a significant shift of the pattern index to lower values that matched both younger and older animals.
source: Similarly, PSS inactivation resulted in a significant shift of the pattern index to lower values (p=0.01) that matched both younger and older animals (see Table 1 for statistics).
evidence: Based on experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 6B and Table 1

claim: A sham PSS injection without muscimol did not impact V1 relative plaid responses or pattern indices.
source: A sham PSS injection without muscimol (Figure 6C,D) did not impact V1 relative plaid responses or pattern indices (see Table 1 for statistics), confirming that PSS inactivation, rather than side effects of the injection, caused the observed V1 effects.
evidence: Based on experimental data from control experiments shown in Figure 6C,D and Table 1

claim: PSS inactivation, rather than side effects of the injection, caused the observed V1 effects.
source: A sham PSS injection without muscimol (Figure 6C,D) did not impact V1 relative plaid responses or pattern indices (see Table 1 for statistics), confirming that PSS inactivation, rather than side effects of the injection, caused the observed V1 effects.
evidence: Based on experimental data from control experiments shown in Figure 6C,D and Table 1

claim: Both changes in V1 plaid responses are at least partially dependent on feedback from PSS.
source: Thus, both changes in V1 plaid responses are at least partially dependent on feedback from PSS.
evidence: Based on experimental data from PSS inactivation experiments

claim: A two-stage model consisting of V1-like local direction filters followed by a PSS-like integration stage could fit well to neural responses in PSS.
source: We have previously shown that a two-stage model consisting of V1-like local direction filters followed by a PSS-like integration stage could fit well to neural responses in PSS (Lempel and Nielsen, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Lempel and Nielsen, 2019)

claim: The model was well able to fit PSS neurons of different types at both ages.
source: As illustrated by the example pattern and component cells shown in Figure 7B, the model was well able to fit PSS neurons of different types at both ages.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 7B

claim: There was generally high correlation between modeled and measured data for both groups.
source: This was further confirmed by a generally high correlation between modeled and measured data for both groups, with little differences between the groups (Figure 7C).
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 7C

claim: For both age groups predicted and measured pattern indices generally matched well.
source: For both age groups predicted and measured pattern indices generally matched well (Figure 7D).
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 7D

claim: The model generally overestimated the absolute value of a neuron's pattern index.
source: While the model generally overestimated the absolute value of a neuron's pattern index, likely because of lower noise levels in the modeled responses, pattern cells remained classified as pattern cells based on the model fits, and component cells remained classified as component cells.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 7D

claim: Winh significantly increased between P37–40 and P44–47.
source: At the same time, Winh significantly increased between the two groups (p<0.001).
evidence: Based on modeling results and statistical analysis shown in Figure 7E

claim: TPSS remained unchanged between P37–40 and P44–47.
source: TPSS, finally, remained unchanged.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 7E

claim: The model results suggest that changes in PSS null direction inhibition are a major component of motion integration development.
source: Thus, the model results suggest that changes in PSS null direction inhibition are a major component of motion integration development.
evidence: Based on modeling results and analysis

claim: Increasing PSS inhibition resulted in a large overall increase in pattern indices.
source: These figures demonstrate that while increasing PSS inhibition resulted in a large overall increase in pattern indices, it came with reduced plaid responses.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8B

claim: Increasing PSS inhibition came with reduced plaid responses.
source: These figures demonstrate that while increasing PSS inhibition resulted in a large overall increase in pattern indices, it came with reduced plaid responses.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8B

claim: Increasing excitation decreased the pattern index by diminishing differences between pattern and component responses.
source: Increasing excitation actually decreased the pattern index by diminishing differences between pattern and component responses, but as expected, the strength of pattern responses was increased across all dOri values.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8C

claim: Increasing excitation increased the strength of pattern responses across all dOri values.
source: Increasing excitation actually decreased the pattern index by diminishing differences between pattern and component responses, but as expected, the strength of pattern responses was increased across all dOri values.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8C

claim: Changing the V1 stage on its own had little consequences on PSS pattern indices.
source: We found that changing the V1 stage on its own had little consequences on PSS pattern indices, which remained largely unchanged from the P37–40 baseline model.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8D

claim: The selective increases in V1 pattern responses propagated to PSS and resulted in increased responses for pattern motion for plaids with intermediate dOri values.
source: However, there were changes in the PSS response to plaids. The selective increases in V1 pattern responses indeed propagated to PSS and resulted in increased responses for pattern motion for plaids with intermediate dOri values.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8D

claim: Increases in PSS excitation, combined with the changes in V1 plaid responses, mitigated the side effects of the increased suppression levels.
source: At the same time, increases in PSS excitation, combined with the changes in V1 plaid responses, mitigated the side effects of the increased suppression levels by limiting them to the component responses only.
evidence: Based on modeling results shown in Figure 8E

claim: Motion tuning functions develop according to their complexity.
source: On a basic level, our data reveal that motion tuning functions develop according to their complexity: Direction selectivity in V1 and PSS matured before motion integration.
evidence: Based on experimental data from the manuscript

claim: Direction selectivity in V1 and PSS matured before motion integration.
source: On a basic level, our data reveal that motion tuning functions develop according to their complexity: Direction selectivity in V1 and PSS matured before motion integration.
evidence: Based on experimental data from the manuscript

claim: MT pattern cells develop slowly, over the course of months, after direction selectivity develops in primates.
source: This matches findings in the primate, in which MT pattern cells also develop slowly, over the course of months, after direction selectivity develops (Chino et al., 1997; Kiorpes and Movshon, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Chino et al., 1997; Kiorpes and Movshon, 2014)

claim: Visual experience is required for normal development of direction selectivity in V1 in both ferrets and cats.
source: In both ferrets and cats, visual experience is required for normal development of direction selectivity in V1 (Li et al., 2008; Blakemore and Van Sluyters, 1975; Cynader et al., 1976).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Li et al., 2008; Blakemore and Van Sluyters, 1975; Cynader et al., 1976)

claim: Rearing cats in a stroboscopic environment results in the loss of direction selectivity in higher area PMLS.
source: At least the basic functions in higher areas are also susceptible to a lack of normal visual experience: Rearing cats in a stroboscopic environment, in which normal motion cues are removed, results in the loss of direction selectivity in higher area PMLS (Spear et al., 1985).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Spear et al., 1985)

claim: Dark reared cats have marked deficits in a behavioral motion integration task.
source: However, our findings are consistent with the observation that dark reared cats have marked deficits in a behavioral motion integration task (Mitchell et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Mitchell et al., 2009)

claim: Neurons in MT of amblyopic monkeys show no changes in pattern responses for plaids.
source: At this time, evidence for a role of visual experience on these functions is mixed: Neurons in MT of amblyopic monkeys show no changes in pattern responses for plaids, but changes in global motion processing were observed when using random dot kinematograms (RDK) (El-Shamayleh et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (El-Shamayleh et al., 2010)

claim: Changes in global motion processing were observed in MT of amblyopic monkeys when using random dot kinematograms.
source: At this time, evidence for a role of visual experience on these functions is mixed: Neurons in MT of amblyopic monkeys show no changes in pattern responses for plaids, but changes in global motion processing were observed when using random dot kinematograms (RDK) (El-Shamayleh et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (El-Shamayleh et al., 2010)

claim: Bilateral congenital cataracts cause large deficits in motion integration performance for RDK in humans.
source: Indeed, bilateral congenital cataracts cause large deficits in motion integration performance for RDK in humans, but deficits after monocular cataracts are much smaller (Ellemberg et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Ellemberg et al., 2002)

claim: Deficits in motion integration performance after monocular cataracts are much smaller than after bilateral cataracts in humans.
source: Indeed, bilateral congenital cataracts cause large deficits in motion integration performance for RDK in humans, but deficits after monocular cataracts are much smaller (Ellemberg et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Ellemberg et al., 2002)

claim: The developmental change in dOri dependency of PSS responses likely reflects at least in part the maturation of motion integration mechanisms.
source: However, the developmental change in dOri dependency of PSS responses likely reflects at least in part the maturation of motion integration mechanisms.
evidence: Based on experimental data and logical inference

claim: An increase in response to plaids with smaller to intermediate dOri values is consistent with increasingly stronger interactions between different motion signals that are pooled together to compute pattern motion.
source: An increase in response to plaids with smaller to intermediate dOri values, for example, is consistent with increasingly stronger interactions between different motion signals that are pooled together to compute pattern motion.
evidence: Based on experimental data and logical inference

claim: Plaid responses became stronger especially in pattern cells throughout development.
source: This conclusion is further supported by the observation that plaid responses became stronger especially in pattern cells throughout development.
evidence: Based on experimental data

claim: Cross-orientation inhibition has previously been studied for 90 deg plaids in ferret V1, both at P40 and in adult animals.
source: Cross-orientation inhibition has previously been studied for 90 deg plaids in ferret V1, both at P40 and in adult animals (Popović et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Popović et al., 2018)

claim: The current data show similar levels of cross-orientation inhibition around P40 as the previous study by Popovic et al.
source: Using the same metric, we observe similar levels of cross-orientation inhibition around P40 (in the new metric, our data has a mean of 0.21 for plaids with dOri = 90 deg).
evidence: Based on experimental data compared to previous work (Popović et al., 2018)

claim: The current data diverge strongly from the previous study by Popovic et al. for adult animals.
source: However, the two data sets diverge strongly for adult animals. While our data show a strong increase, Popovic et al. report a small but significant decrease in cross-orientation inhibition.
evidence: Based on experimental data compared to previous work (Popović et al., 2018)

claim: The discrepancy between the current data and the previous study may be due to differences in the sampled neuronal population.
source: This discrepancy may be due to differences in the sampled neuronal population (in terms of laminar location or location within V1), but it is more likely caused by differences in the stimulus presentation protocol (slower presentation of individual stimuli versus fast presentation embedded in a train of stimuli).
evidence: Based on speculation about possible causes of the discrepancy

claim: The discrepancy between the current data and the previous study is more likely caused by differences in the stimulus presentation protocol.
source: This discrepancy may be due to differences in the sampled neuronal population (in terms of laminar location or location within V1), but it is more likely caused by differences in the stimulus presentation protocol (slower presentation of individual stimuli versus fast presentation embedded in a train of stimuli).
evidence: Based on speculation about possible causes of the discrepancy

claim: The model results show that the changes in V1 responses can complement changes in PSS-internal motion integration mechanisms in a meaningful manner.
source: Our model suggests a possible role for the temporary V1 changes we observed. More precisely, the model results show that the changes in V1 responses can complement changes in PSS-internal motion integration mechanisms in a meaningful manner.
evidence: Based on modeling results

claim: The model was motivated by the importance of null direction inhibition in motion computations in ferret V1.
source: We modeled PSS motion integration by using a weight function with an excitatory component centered at the preferred direction, and an inhibitory component centered at the null direction. This was motivated by the importance of null direction inhibition in motion computations in ferret V1 (Wilson et al., 2018), but it also matches the shape of MT motion integration functions as estimated by fitting a primate motion pathway model to plaid responses (Rust et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Wilson et al., 2018)

claim: The model matches the shape of MT motion integration functions as estimated by fitting a primate motion pathway model to plaid responses.
source: We modeled PSS motion integration by using a weight function with an excitatory component centered at the preferred direction, and an inhibitory component centered at the null direction. This was motivated by the importance of null direction inhibition in motion computations in ferret V1 (Wilson et al., 2018), but it also matches the shape of MT motion integration functions as estimated by fitting a primate motion pathway model to plaid responses (Rust et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Rust et al., 2006)

claim: Inhibition proved to be the strongest contributor to improving motion integration in the model.
source: Inhibition proved to be the strongest contributor to improving motion integration.
evidence: Based on modeling results

claim: The model makes the testable prediction that inhibitory circuits in PSS should mature relatively slowly, not before P40.
source: Our model therefore makes the testable prediction that inhibitory circuits in PSS should mature relatively slowly, not before P40.
evidence: Based on modeling results and logical inference

claim: Inhibitory circuits in ferret V1 have been found to develop up to P60.
source: No data exist for inhibitory circuit development in PSS, but inhibitory circuits in ferret V1 have been found to develop up to P60 both in terms of the relative proportion of different types of inhibitory neurons, as well as their laminar distribution (Chen et al., 2005; Dalva, 2010; Gao et al., 1999; Gao et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Chen et al., 2005; Dalva, 2010; Gao et al., 1999; Gao et al., 2000)

claim: A similarly slow development of inhibitory circuity in PSS appears possible.
source: A similarly slow development of inhibitory circuity in PSS does therefore appear possible.
evidence: Based on logical inference from the development of inhibitory circuits in V1

claim: The unwanted suppression of pattern responses occurs in particular for plaids with intermediate dOri values.
source: The unwanted suppression of pattern responses occurs in particular for plaids with intermediate dOri values.
evidence: Based on modeling results

claim: To increase the responses to plaids with intermediate dOri values, the excitatory component would need to increase in width.
source: To increase the responses to these plaids, the excitatory component would need to increase in width – but the broader this part of the weight function, the broader the resulting direction tuning function even for simple stimuli like gratings.
evidence: Based on logical inference from the model structure

claim: The broader the excitatory component of the weight function, the broader the resulting direction tuning function even for simple stimuli like gratings.
source: To increase the responses to these plaids, the excitatory component would need to increase in width – but the broader this part of the weight function, the broader the resulting direction tuning function even for simple stimuli like gratings.

claim: By dividing the 'workload' of increasing pattern responses between V1 and PSS, the increases in the excitatory weight function in PSS can be kept to a reasonable level.
source: By dividing the 'workload' of increasing pattern responses between V1 and PSS, the increases in the excitatory weight function in PSS can be kept to a reasonable level.
evidence: Based on modeling results and logical inference

claim: V1 selectively contributes to strengthening responses to the plaid conditions most important for pattern motion computations.
source: Thus, independent of the exact implementation of the motion pathway model, V1 selectively contributes to strengthening responses to the plaid conditions most important for pattern motion computations.
evidence: Based on modeling results and logical inference

claim: If V1 changes are indeed temporary, it would suggest that other mechanisms eventually replace the V1 contribution.
source: If V1 changes are indeed temporary, it would suggest that other mechanisms – originating either in PSS or elsewhere – eventually replace the V1 contribution.
evidence: Based on speculation about the implications of temporary V1 changes

claim: V1 changes may actually be permanent, but become limited to the subgroup of neurons that project from V1 to PSS.
source: Alternatively, V1 changes may actually be permanent, but become limited to the subgroup of neurons that project from V1 to PSS, similar to the other specializations that have been reported for the V1 neurons participating in the motion pathway (Jarosiewicz et al., 2012; Movshon and Newsome, 1996).
evidence: Based on speculation and citations to previous work (Jarosiewicz et al., 2012; Movshon and Newsome, 1996)

claim: PSS may actively adjust V1 signals to (temporarily) aid its own development.
source: In one scenario, PSS actively adjusts V1 signals to (temporarily) aid its own development.
evidence: Based on speculation about the implications of V1 changes depending on PSS feedback

claim: V1 changes may be a (more passive) consequence of the change in PSS feedback signals that arises from the newly developed PSS functions.
source: In the other, V1 changes are a (more passive) consequence of the change in PSS feedback signals that arises from the newly developed PSS functions.
evidence: Based on speculation about the implications of V1 changes depending on PSS feedback

claim: Either scenario links development across multiple network nodes of the motion pathway.
source: Either scenarios link development across multiple network nodes of the motion pathway, and are important concepts for studying the development of a cortical pathway.
evidence: Based on logical inference from the experimental findings
